title: Garden Window Safari
teaser: The best show in town is playing just outside, and you have front-row seats.
clue: A quiet hide, a few supplies and the whole outdoors on the other side of the glass.
reveal: You build a cozy hide at a window or open doorway and bring the garden to your dog's nose, with scent finds on the blanket and a feeder that draws visitors.
objective: Settle your dog in a sheltered hide at a window or doorway and enjoy the sights, sounds and smells of the outdoors together.
instructions: A day or two ahead, put a small bird feeder or a dish of birdseed outside the window, a few meters from the glass and well out of your dog's reach.

Make the hide: a bed or blanket at the window or doorway, with a chair beside it. If you use an open doorway, keep your dog on a leash or behind a baby gate so they cannot bolt. Check the floor is non-slip, the window is secure and the view is calm.

Make the Ranger's Picnic: scatter four or five pieces of usual food, or tuck a scent cloth under the blanket corner, so your dog has a find the moment they arrive. Keep a second scent cloth in your pocket for later.
Settle in and open the window a crack if the weather is mild, so the smells and sounds of outside come in. Whisper, keep still and let your dog look, sniff or doze.

When something appears, a bird, a leaf blown past, a neighbor's cat, a squirrel, make a tally mark on a paper card as a 'sighting'. Nothing needs to be found for it to count. After the first visitor, slide out the second scent cloth as the Ranger's Reward.
End with a nap in the hide. Count the tally, name the Visitor of the Day on the card, and leave the feeder up and the hide in place for a repeat visit tomorrow.
twist: You bring the safari to your dog: scent finds on the hide blanket, a reward when the first visitor arrives, and a feeder that sends visitors to the glass.
variations: Puppy: keep it to five minutes in a doorway on your lap, with your puppy indoors.
No feeder: watch the street, the clouds and the breeze.
Seated owner: put the chair and bed side by side at the glass door.
Fretful watcher: close the curtains halfway and swap to the picnic scent finds.
completion: You have settled in the hide for a while and your dog has had a sniff, a look or a snooze there.
photoIdea: The hide at golden hour with a visitor in the background, or your dog's ears pointed to the window. No posing.
memoryPrompt: Who visited the feeder, and what did your dog make of the sightings?
optionalSupplies: A few pieces of usual food
substitutes: No feeder? A shallow dish of water for birds.
No card? Notes on your phone.
dietNotes: Use only a few pieces of the usual diet, or use a scent cloth. Keep birdseed away from your dog, and ask your vet about diet.
safety: Keep your dog on the floor, never on a sill, and keep windows secure or screened.
If your dog barks or fixates at the glass, close the curtains and try again another day.
Puppies stay indoors until your vet says public places are fine; keep seed and feeders out of reach.

keepsake.explainer: Went on safari without leaving the blanket
